item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht

item.content:encoded:
Ather’s Profit Milestone Meets A Manufacturing Crunch 

Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy turned its maiden profit in Q2 FY27, and now plans to sustain its growth momentum via accelerated investments in its manufacturing capabilities as demand continues to outpace its production. 

Let’s steal a glance at the OEM’s Q2 FY27 numbers:

  • Net profit of ₹1.3 Cr against a net loss of ₹154.1 Cr in Q2 FY26
  • Operating revenue climbed 62.9% to ₹1,464.2 Cr, up 20.3% QoQ
  • EBITDA profit widened to ₹74.2 Cr from ₹9 Cr a year ago
  • Sales of scooters rose 42% YoY to 93,211 units

Other Income Drives Maiden Profit: After 13 years of innovating EV technology, Ather Energy posted its first-ever profitable quarter after turning EBITDA profitable in the preceding quarter as revenue growth far outpaced expenses, which rose 39.4% YoY to ₹1,526 Cr.  However, its operating revenue was ₹61.5 Cr lower than total expenses during the quarter, and the difference was plugged by other income, highlighting a continued quest to improve profitability margins. 

Manufacturing Boost On The Cards: The OEM will invest ₹122 Cr to add 2.25 Lakh units annually to its manufacturing capacity. Its under-construction Factory 3.0 in Maharashtra will receive ₹64 Cr to add 1.5 Lakh units of annual capacity over the planned 5 Lakh units. At its Hosur plant, Ather will invest ₹53 Cr to add capacity for 75,000 units and also set up a new battery line to offset supply chain worries. 

Ather Bleeds On Demand Front: The EV maker believes that it is losing 18,000-20,000 units in demand monthly due to its supply shortfall, with the Hosur plant now operating at 98% capacity and Factory 3.0 yet to go live. This comes as customer enquiries surged 109% YoY to around 10 Lakh, and pre-orders more than doubled to 1.8 Lakh. 

With demand outpacing production and factories nearing capacity, its next challenge is to keep the growth engine running. While we will keep an eye out for just that, here’s how Ather Energy fared in the second quarter of FY27.

From The Editor’s Desk

 Paytm’s Profit Spree

  • The fintech major’s Q2 FY27 net profit surged 10.7X YoY to ₹225 Cr from ₹21 Cr a year ago, edging up from ₹220 Cr in Q1 FY27.
  • Operating revenue grew 28% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹2,648 Cr, while total expenses rose 23% YoY to ₹2,531 Cr.
  • Paytm’s profitability gains follow a strong Q1 FY27, when net profit rose 78.8% YoY to ₹220 Cr and EBITDA profit jumped 182% to ₹203 Cr, with an EBITDA margin of 8%.

 Imarticus To File ₹1,000 Cr IPO Soon

  • The edtech startup is planning to file its DRHP with SEBI through the confidential route in the next two to three months for a ₹1,000 Cr IPO, up from its earlier ₹750 Cr plan.
  • The company plans to use the proceeds to expand its business, set up more Centres of Excellence, strengthen its School of Finance and Business and B2B operations, and pursue acquisitions. This follows its recent ₹800 Cr acquisition of Singapore’s BELLS Institute of Higher Learning.
  • The IPO plans come amid a slowdown in edtech funding and growing consolidation, with upGrad recently acquiring Unacademy in a deal valuing the startup at just over $200 Mn, down more than 90% from its peak valuation of $3.5 Bn.

 Unacademy Cofounders’ ₹700 Cr VC Play 

  • Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are raising ₹700 Cr for Longshot Capital, an early stage fund that has secured ₹250-300 Cr in commitments and is targeting its first close in January 2027.
  • The Bengaluru-based fund plans to back 25-28 AI and deeptech startups at the seed and pre-Series A stages, with initial cheques of 500K-1.5 Mn across sectors such as manufacturing, space, defence and robotics.
  • The move follows upGrad’s acquisition of Unacademy in an all-stock deal valuing the edtech startup at ₹1,955 Cr, over 90% below its peak valuation. The fund also builds on the founders’ track record of over 200 angel investments worth more than ₹25 Cr.

Pronto Founder Finds Her New Gig In AI

  • Anjali Sardana has launched an AI venture, Provision Labs, to collect real-world data for training and testing AI systems designed to perform physical tasks using robots and machines.
  • The launch follows scrutiny over Pronto’s pilot that involved recording household chores to generate robotics training data, raising concerns around customer consent, data privacy and the use of footage.
  • Provision Labs enters a growing market for real-world AI training data, with startups such as Human Archive, Awign and Objectways building pipelines to supply footage of human activities to AI and robotics developers.

Aequs Bloats Its Losses In Q2

  • The contract manufacturer reported a consolidated net loss of ₹52.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, widening 154.4% YoY from ₹20.6 Cr. It reported a net loss of ₹53.2 Cr in Q1.
  • Operating revenue grew 45.3% YoY to ₹409.1 Cr, led by its aerospace business, which contributed ₹351.4 Cr, while consumer business revenue rose 52% to ₹57.7 Cr.
  • Expenses excluding finance costs, depreciation and amortisation surged 56.2% to ₹395.2 Cr, outpacing revenue growth. Sequentially, the net loss narrowed marginally from ₹53.2 Cr in Q1 FY27.

AI Trading Platform Tradl Raises $4.1 Mn 

  • Bengaluru-based Tradl raised $4.1 Mn in a seed round led by Nexus Venture Partners and Stellaris Venture Partners, with participation from angel investors.
  • Founded in 2025 by IIT Guwahati graduates Shubham Bansal and Nilesh Raj, Tradl combines AI and quantitative analysis to help retail traders screen stocks, analyse markets, and backtest strategies.
  • The fundraise comes amid rising investor interest in AI startups, with the segment attracting $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

Inside Pulse’s Bet To Make Medical Equipment In India

India’s hospitals remain dependent on imported medical devices that can be costly, difficult to service and poorly adapted to local needs. Pulse is trying to build a domestic alternative by combining MSME manufacturing with product design under a single medtech brand.

Going Asset-Light: Founded in 2025, Pulse designs, sources and supplies medical devices and consumables. Instead of owning a large manufacturing base, it provides engineering, product standardisation, certifications, regulatory compliance and service infrastructure to small businesses. This enables these SMEs to build medical equipment that can compete with global manufacturers. 

The Essential Approach: Pulse is initially targeting low- and mid-complexity devices across critical care, renal care and cardiac care. The company is also focusing on mid-tier hospitals, particularly facilities with 50-200 beds, where reliable equipment at accessible prices can have a direct impact on healthcare delivery. 

The Quality Layer: The startup currently works with nearly 20 MSME partners across Delhi NCR, Gujarat, Kolkata and Mumbai. It is also establishing an R&D hub at the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone in Visakhapatnam. Going forward, the 3one4 Capital-backed startup plans to scale product development and distribution. 

As hospitals seek affordable and dependable alternatives to imported equipment, can Pulse turn India into a medtech manufacturing hub?

item.title: Protectt.ai To Acquire Controlling Stake In Bosch’s AIShield
item.dc:creator: Shraddha Goled
item.description: AI-native cybersecurity startup Protectt.ai plans to acquire a controlling stake in AIShield, an AI security platform incubated within Bosch Global…
item.content:encoded:
AI-native cybersecurity startup Protectt.ai plans to acquire a controlling stake in AIShield, an AI security platform incubated within Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW). Bosch will retain a minority stake in AIShield following the transaction.

Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Protectt.ai will acquire the stake through a deal comprising primary and secondary components. The companies have not disclosed the transaction value or timeline.

“There will be cash, a secondary component and future investments as required. The current structure is a combination of cash and ESOPs. Future investments will depend on the requirements of the business,” Protectt.ai cofounder Manish Mimani told Inc42.

Founded in 2022 by Shiv Kumar and Amit Phadke, AIShield was incubated within BGSW. It develops security solutions for machine learning models, generative AI applications and AI supply chains, helping enterprises defend against attacks designed to manipulate AI systems and address compliance risks.

The partnership will combine AIShield’s AI security capabilities with Protectt.ai’s mobile security platform, allowing the latter to expand into enterprise AI security.

AIShield will continue to operate as an independent entity under Protectt.ai once the deal is completed, with its own professional management team and a focus on AI security research and product development. It will also be able to raise external funding in the future.

Protectt.ai plans to work with private companies and government organisations through AIShield to build an India-developed AI security platform, Mimani said.

From Mobile Security To Enterprise AI

Founded in 2020 by Manish Mimani and Mohanraj Selvaraj, Protectt.ai provides mobile threat defence solutions that help businesses protect applications against cyber threats and fraud. Its platform also serves as a compliance hub for app owners, helping them adhere to regulations issued by entities such as the RBI, SEBI and NPCI.

The startup also offers a full-stack AI security platform with tools to test AI agents for vulnerabilities, secure connections between AI applications and external tools, and monitor AI agents while they operate.

Protectt.ai’s security technology runs on more than 1 Bn mobile devices and processes 15 Bn mobile application sessions every month, Mimani said.

He expects mobile applications to increasingly rely on AI agents to perform tasks, potentially reducing the need for users to navigate conventional app interfaces over the next one to two years.

Protectt.ai had already been researching AI model scanning and AI agent security as part of its product roadmap. Through the AIShield acquisition, the startup aims to extend these capabilities beyond mobile applications to enterprise use cases across sectors.

Some members of Protectt.ai’s AI security team will move to AIShield, although the number has yet to be finalised.

AIShield currently has around 12–15 employees and plans to expand its team to 50–60 people by March 2027. It plans to hire PhD researchers, master’s graduates and other technical talent from leading institutions to strengthen its research and engineering capabilities.

The team will focus on developing products, conducting research and filing patents, Mimani said.

Protectt.ai Eyes Further Acquisitions

The AIShield deal is Protectt.ai’s first such acquisition. The startup set up an M&A team earlier in 2026 to evaluate potential acquisitions and partnerships, with a focus on building capabilities and addressing gaps in its existing offerings.

Protectt.ai is exploring opportunities in areas such as API security and cloud security that could complement its current capabilities, Mimani said.

The startup secured around $16 Mn in a Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Bajaj Finance in 2025. Mimani added that Protectt.ai is evaluating opportunities and expects to consider raising fresh funds in 2027.

item.title: News Publishers Move SC To Challenge The DPDP Act
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: A group of 21 news publishers has reportedly challenged India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act in the Supreme Court…
item.content:encoded:
A group of 21 news publishers has reportedly challenged India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act in the Supreme Court (SC), arguing that the law could undermine investigative journalism and expose journalists’ sources.

The lawsuit, filed on October 6, argues that the law’s provisions on consent, data erasure and government access to information could restrict news reporting and force publishers to remove factual stories. The case is scheduled to be heard on October 27, according to a Reuters report.

The challenge comes nearly a year after the Centre notified the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 in November last year. The broader DPDP Act, 2023 and the Rules establish a framework governing how organisations collect, process and protect individuals’ digital personal data.

The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), which represents the publishers, has argued that the law does not provide a specific exemption for journalistic activities. According to the confidential filing, the association reportedly said that the absence of such safeguards could compromise press freedom and investigative reporting.

The DNPA’s members include Mukesh Ambani-owned Network18, Gautam Adani-owned NDTV, the Indian Express and Times Internet, which is part of the Times of India group.

Publishers Vs The DPDP Act

A key concern raised by the publishers is the requirement to obtain consent before processing personal data. The DNPA has argued that requiring journalists to notify the subjects of investigations and seek their consent could allow them to destroy evidence or intimidate witnesses.

The association has also flagged provisions allowing individuals to withdraw consent and request the erasure of their personal data. According to the filing, the absence of a public-interest safeguard could force publishers to remove or substantially redact factual news reports.

The publishers have further raised concerns about provisions empowering the government to seek information from organisations handling personal data. They argue that these powers could expose confidential journalistic sources and discourage whistleblowers from sharing information about corruption, corporate wrongdoing and electoral malpractice.

The filing also challenges the government’s power to restrict access to information in the public interest, arguing that the provisions could curtail press freedom.

The DNPA has sought the quashing of several contentious provisions of the law, most of which are scheduled to come into effect from May 2027, Reuters reported.

The association has also argued that the government has granted broad exemptions to the state without extending corresponding protections to the press.

What The DPDP Framework Provides

The DPDP Act, enacted in August 2023, establishes obligations for processing digital personal data. The later DPDP Rules, notified in November 2025, provide a phased implementation framework, giving organisations up to 18 months to comply with specified requirements.

The framework requires platforms to obtain consent for processing personal data, provide clear information about its use and implement security safeguards. It also gives individuals rights to access, correct, update and seek the erasure of their personal data, subject to the applicable provisions.

The latest case marks one of the most prominent challenges to the DPDP framework so far, raising questions about how India’s data protection requirements will interact with press freedom and investigative reporting.

The Act provides for financial penalties of up to ₹250 Cr for failing to implement reasonable security safeguards. Other violations, including certain breaches of obligations relating to children’s personal data, can attract penalties of up to ₹200 Cr.

However, the publishers argue that the framework does not adequately account for the requirements of investigative journalism, particularly when reporting involves personal information collected in the public interest.

The government has maintained that the framework protects citizens’ privacy while supporting responsible data processing.

item.title: BioStack Nets $9.5 Mn To Build Training Datasets For Medical AI
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: AI-powered healthtech platform BioStack has raised $9.5 Mn (₹90.4 Cr) in its seed funding round led by Peak XV Partners,…
item.content:encoded:
AI-powered healthtech platform BioStack has raised $9.5 Mn (₹90.4 Cr) in its seed funding round led by Peak XV Partners, Afore Capital, DCVC, Emerson Collective, SV Angel, Verdict Capital, Streamlined Ventures, and Y Combinator. 

The startup plans to utilise the fresh capital to continue expanding its presence in the US and other international markets, including India, Brazil, and Argentina. A chunk of the capital will also be used to scale its tech stack and ramp up hiring across engineering and research teams.

Founded in 2025 by Sanat Mishra and Parth Patwa, BioStack claims to be building the data infrastructure for the next generation of medical AI. 

It combines fragmented clinical information across systems such as electronic health records, medical imaging, clinical notes and medications. The startup then uses this data to create proprietary datasets for research, biotechnology, and the development and training of medical AI models.

“We’re building the infrastructure that connects all of the clinical information and makes it useful, both for clinicians making decisions today and for the researchers and AI developers building the future of medicine,” said BioStack cofounder and CEO Mishra.

BioStack currently works with multiple hospitals across the US, Brazil and Argentina. In India, it is also connecting cancer patients with an investigational cancer vaccine program. 

The startup also claims that it offers use cases such as AI model evaluation, disease modeling, biomarker discovery, patient stratification and treatment-response analysis.

Besides offering custom workflows to protect patient privacy, the startup claims to have so far processed 10 Cr de-identified patient records, more than “several hundred thousand” fragmented X-Rays, MRIs and CT scans, and “several million” telehealth audio transcripts. 

For context, de-identified patient records are medical datasets that have had all personal and direct identifiers removed so that the individual cannot reasonably be linked to the data.

The fundraise comes as India becomes a training ground to collect datasets for powering AI models and physical AI products. Startups are tapping India’s huge population to collect recordings of workers performing physical tasks, processing the footage, and selling the resulting datasets to frontier AI labs and robotics companies.

For instance, the likes of Awign, Objectways and Human Archive are building pipelines to supply first-person footage of human activity to AI developers. Just a day ago, instant home services startup Pronto’s founder Anjali Sardana launched Provision Labs, a US-based venture to collect data for physical AI systems.

At the heart of all this is the Indian AI training dataset, which is projected to become a $1.3 Bn opportunity by 2033.

item.title: Matiks Bags $10 Mn To Take Its Puzzle Gaming Platform Global
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Social gaming platform Matiks has raised $10 Mn (₹95.1 Cr) in its Pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst. …
item.content:encoded:
Social gaming platform Matiks has raised $10 Mn (₹95.1 Cr) in its Pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst. 

The round also saw participation from upGrad founder Ronnie Screwvala as well as existing backers such as Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners and Untitled Ventures.

In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to expand its global footprint and invest in new games and social experiences. The fresh funding will also be used to deepen investments in engineering, AI, product, design and growth. 

A chunk of the capital will also be utilised to build an AI-powered engine, which will enable users to build and publish their own social games without writing code. Going forward, it has also set its eyes on scaling creator partnerships, global distribution and player community.

“… We started Matiks with a simple belief: using your brain can be just as fun and addictive as any other form of entertainment. Our ambition is to make mind sports as culturally relevant as physical sports and esports – giving mental athletes, puzzlers, and competitive players the visibility, communities, and recognition they deserve…,” said Matiks cofounder and CEO Sudhanshu Bhatia.

Founded in 2024 by Bhatia, Mohan Kumar and Sushant Timmapur, Matiks is an esports platform that allows users to play social games spanning mathematics, memory, logic and puzzles. It also allows users to compete with each other. 

The startup claims that more than 22 Lakh players had played 4.8 Cr games on its platform as of September 2026. Matiks also claimed that its daily active users currently hover around 3 Lakh, with early engagement also emerging from international markets such as Japan, the US and South Korea.

The startup last raised $3.14 Mn in its pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Ventures in August last year.

Going forward, the startup plans to initially prioritise expansion in the US before entering more tier I markets. Its future roadmap also includes building its AI-powered game creation engine, which the startup believes will foster adoption and create new experiences.

The fundraise comes as India’s gaming market is expanding beyond the usual battle royale and casual games. Buoyed by 51 Cr gamers, the ban on real-money games last year, the rise of AI and regulatory push for social games, the homegrown gaming arena is seeing renewed traction and interest from investors.

Earlier this month, mobile gaming studio Spill Games raised $10.5 Mn in its Series A round led by Elevation Capital. In April this year, another gaming studio LightFury Games also bagged $11 Mn in its pre-Series A funding round from Blume Ventures and others.

In August, cricketer Rohit Sharma also joined LightFury Games as an investor, alongside MS Dhoni, Jasprit Bumrah, and Hardik Pandya, among others. 

At the heart of all this is the Indian gaming market, which is projected to become a $9.9 Bn opportunity by 2031.

item.title: LEAP India Q2: Profit Zooms 62% YoY To ₹18 Cr, Revenue Up 18%
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Logistics company LEAP India reported a net profit of ₹17.8 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 62% from nearly ₹11 Cr…
item.content:encoded:
Logistics company LEAP India reported a net profit of ₹17.8 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 62% from nearly ₹11 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, the company’s profit dipped 28% from ₹24.7 Cr in Q1 FY27.

The company’s EBITDA rose 25% YoY to ₹109.7 Cr, with the EBITDA margin expanding 91 basis points to 50.8%.

The company’s profit was impacted by a one-time charge of ₹6.8 Cr for prepayment of long-term borrowings.

Meanwhile, operating revenue jumped 18.2% to ₹211.2 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹178.7 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a QoQ basis, the company’s top line remained largely flat and rose 3.8% from ₹203.4 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Including other income of ₹4.7 Cr, total income for the period stood at ₹215.9 Cr in the quarter under review.

Meanwhile, expenses rose 14.7% to ₹185.2 Cr in Q2 FY27 as against ₹161.5 Cr in the quarter ended September 2025. LEAP India also incurred an additional ₹6 Cr in tax expenses during the quarter.

The company also announced two strategic acquisitions. Through its wholly owned subsidiaries, LEAP signed agreements to acquire the businesses of Vimprotech and Total International Packaging Solutions (TIPS) for a combined consideration of ₹142 Cr. The businesses generated ₹65 Cr in revenue in FY26 and serve more than 200 customers across sectors including electronics, white goods, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, automotive and food and beverages.

Vimprotech brings in-house plastics design, mould-making and manufacturing capabilities across facilities in Puducherry and Tamil Nadu. TIPS adds an automotive container-pooling business with four warehouses across Bengaluru, Nashik and Tirunelveli. The acquisitions are expected to strengthen backward integration, reduce reliance on external suppliers and create cross-selling opportunities for pallets, crates, containers and MHE.

Founded in 2013 by Sunu Mathew, LEAP India provides supply chain solutions spanning equipment pooling, inventory management, transportation, and repair and maintenance. It serves customers across sectors such as FMCG, beverages, ecommerce, automotive and retail.

Asset pooling remained the core growth driver. Income from asset pooling increased 19% YoY in Q2 FY27, while material handling equipment (MHE) income rose 52%. LEAP operates a pool of 15.5 Mn assets valued at over ₹1,820 Cr, serving more than 1,100 customers across 11,000-plus touchpoints and 27 fulfilment centres. Customer churn remained below 0.5%.

Asset utilisation stood at 89.3% for pallets and 82.3% for MHE as of September 2026, while container utilisation improved to 73.7%. LEAP estimates that it commands around 90% of India’s organised pallet-pooling market, which it expects to expand as organised warehousing, supply-chain automation and modern retail drive demand.

LEAP’s balance sheet also strengthened. Net debt nearly halved to ₹433.7 Cr from ₹801 Cr a year earlier, while the debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.48x from 0.96x. Net debt-to-EBITDA declined to around 1.9x from 4.4x.

“Strong growth, continued improvements in cost efficiency and rising profitability position us well to sustain this momentum. With a scalable business model, disciplined execution and a clear focus on operational excellence, we remain confident in our ability to deliver long-term value and strengthen the trust our shareholders have placed in us,” Mathew said.

Shares of LEAP India ended today’s trading session 3.06% higher at ₹126.35  apiece on the BSE.

item.title: AceVector Q2 Loss Surges 116% YoY To ₹16.2 Cr, Revenue Up 17%
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Snapdeal parent AceVector’s net loss for the September quarter (Q2) of FY27 zoomed 116% to ₹16.2 Cr from ₹7.5 Cr…
item.content:encoded:
Snapdeal parent AceVector’s net loss for the September quarter (Q2) of FY27 zoomed 116% to ₹16.2 Cr from ₹7.5 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, the company trimmed its loss by 37% from ₹25.5 Cr. 

Operating revenue increased 17% YoY and 13% QoQ to ₹151.2 Cr. Including other income of ₹2.6 Cr, total income for the quarter stood at ₹153.8 Cr.

Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter also increased 22% YoY to ₹168.7 Cr. Logistics expense was the biggest chunk of expense during the quarter and increased 20% YoY to ₹71.4 Cr. 

AceVector listed on the bourses earlier this month post completing its ₹420 Cr IPO. The company had disclosed its financial performance for the fiscal year FY26 in its IPO papers. 

For the first half of the ongoing fiscal year, the company’s consolidated revenue grew by 17% YoY to ₹285.5 Cr, supported by growth across Snapdeal and Unicommerce. 

In this, both Snapdeal and Unicommerce, AceVector’s primary business engines, registered 15% YoY jump in revenue to ₹164.4 Cr and ₹110.4 Cr, respectively.

Meanwhile, the company’s consolidated Adjusted EBITDA loss for the half stood at ₹26.9 Cr. This is about triple the ₹9.3 Cr adjusted EBITDA loss incurred in H1 FY26. 

AceVector said that the increased loss was due to higher marketing investments in preparation of the festive season and temporary logistics cost pressures at Snapdeal due to macroeconomic factors, alongside investments in Unicommerce to support long-term growth.

Snapdeal’s Operational Performance

Snapdeal’s net merchandise value (NMV) from fashion grew 31% to ₹407.6 Cr in H1 FY27, accounting for 68.4% of the marketplace’s overall NMV. The value fashion platform’s overall NMV rose 10% to ₹595.7 Cr, while delivered units increased 16% to 150.5 lakh.

The growth was driven by rising demand for value fashion and higher app adoption. App-delivered units grew 23% YoY to 133.6 lakh during the half-year, while annual transacting customers increased 12% to 1.31 Cr. Placed order frequency also rose 11% to 4.1 times a year.

However, Snapdeal said the shift in festive shopping to Q3 FY27 moderated its Q2 and H1 growth. Early festive momentum has been encouraging, with units growing 60% YoY in the first half of October.

The company also stepped up marketing investments in Q2 to acquire new users ahead of the festive season. These investments are expected to have an impact in Q3 FY27 as well.

On profitability, Snapdeal’s contribution margin improved to 10.2% of NMV in Q2 FY27 from 8.8% in Q1, as temporary logistics cost pressures eased and monetisation improved. Its Adjusted EBITDA margin also narrowed to -5.2% of NMV in Q2 from -8.5% in Q1, aided by the recovery in contribution margin and lower marketing and fixed expenses as a proportion of NMV.

Snapdeal is positioning itself as a value fashion destination for younger shoppers, with products largely priced between ₹300 and ₹800.

Its zero-commission model is intended to attract a wider seller base, including small manufacturers and regional businesses, while allowing sellers greater flexibility in pricing. Snapdeal said nearly 65% of its new customers are Gen Z shoppers and more than 80% of its sales come from non-metro towns.

Unicommerce Revenue Grows 15%

AceVector’s other key business, ecommerce software provider Unicommerce, reported a 15% YoY increase in H1 FY27 revenue to ₹110.4 Cr from ₹96.3 Cr. Its Adjusted EBITDA, however, declined to ₹16.7 Cr from ₹19.7 Cr as it invested in AI-led product innovation, talent and capacity, particularly across sales and marketing.

Unicommerce added 121 enterprise clients in Q2 FY27, compared with 103 in the year-ago quarter. Its enterprise client additions increased 24% YoY to 236 in H1 FY27 from 191 in H1 FY26.

The company expects profitability to improve in the second half as incremental investments moderate and revenue growth creates operating leverage. It also expects Shipway, its shipping and logistics platform, to return to Adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q3 FY27.

Important to mention that Unicommerce announced its quarterly performance earlier last week. The ecommerce SaaS company eported a consolidated net profit of ₹6.4 Cr in the September quarter while operating revenue grew 15% YoY and QoQ to ₹59.1 Cr during the quarter.

Shares of AceVector ended today’s trading session 0.96% higher at ₹20.93 apiece on the BSE .

item.title: Nazara Swings Back To The Black In Q2, Posts ₹34 Cr Profit
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Gaming major Nazara Technologies swung back to the black in Q2 FY27 and reported a profit of ₹35.4 Cr against…
item.content:encoded:
Gaming major Nazara Technologies swung back to the black in Q2 FY27 and reported a profit of ₹35.4 Cr against a net loss of ₹33.9 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, the bottom line improved from a loss of ₹82.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.

It is pertinent to note that the year-ago loss figures were skewed as the listed gaming company had lodged ₹914.7 Cr in impairment and other losses during the quarter ended September 2025. 

Meanwhile, the profits came on the back of improving margins and operating revenue zooming nearly 52% to ₹803.2 Cr during the quarter under review from ₹526.5 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a QoQ basis, the top line rose 87.3% from ₹428.8 Cr in Q1 FY27.

The company attributed the surge in revenue to Bluetile and BestPlay adding ₹329 Cr to its top line from August 2026 and healthy organic growth across its verticals. 

Including other income of ₹13.7 Cr, Nazara’s total income stood at ₹816.9 Cr in the quarter under review. Meanwhile, total expenses (including the ₹6.7 Cr in impairment expenses) also rose 43.7% to ₹767.6 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹534.3 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. 

In a filing with the exchanges, Nazara said that its EBITDA improved 93% YoY to ₹120 Cr in Q1 FY27, while its EBITDA margin jumped 311 bps YoY to 14.9% in the quarter under review.

“This quarter demonstrates the company we are building: a portfolio of high-quality games on a single, shared platform. Bluetile and BestPlay grew EBITDA 64% in their first two months as part of Nazara, while sustained investment in content delivered organic growth of 11% in revenue and 17% in EBITDA across our existing gaming studios…,” said Nazara CEO Raymond Stauffer.

Nazara’s Gaming Play

As usual, the gaming business accounted for 82% of Nazara’s total revenue at ₹656 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 122% YoY. The vertical’s EBITDA also zoomed 114% YoY to ₹141 Cr on the back of Bluetile and BestPlay consolidation. 

Within gaming, Fusebox’s narrative gaming business, which includes Love Island and Big Brother, saw its revenue decline 4% YoY to ₹107 Cr in Q2 FY27. The company attributed the contraction to lower organic installs and the global decline in similar mobile game downloads. Despite the contraction, EBITDA improved 7% YoY at ₹126 Cr during the quarter.

Kiddopia’s top line rose 21% YoY to ₹57 Cr in the quarter under review, while average revenue per user (ARPU) jumped 8% YoY to $7.94 (around ₹756). However, EBITDA declined by a massive 77% YoY to ₹103 Cr as Kiddopia stepped up user acquisition spending to accelerate subscriber growth.

“Kiddopia revenue grew 21% YoY as subscribers rose 5% and ARPU rose 8% to $7.94. EBITDA declined as Kiddopia stepped up user acquisition spend to accelerate subscriber growth, while keeping unit economics within our target thresholds,” read Nazara’s investor presentation.

The stars of the show were Bluetile and BestPlay that together reported a gross revenue of ₹329 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 49% YoY, against an EBITDA of ₹64 Cr, also up 64% YoY. Nazara attributed this to rapid updates, new features, live events, automation and strong adoption in new countries.

“Sharpened EBITDA focus while fully automating campaign management, App Store optimisation, and creative pipelines via AI… Heavily reallocated capacity across all departments following proprietary AI breakthroughs,” added Nazara on Bluetile and BestPlay’s performance.

The listed gaming giant’s offline business, spanning Funky Monkeys and Smaaash, reported a revenue of ₹29 Cr during the quarter, down from ₹30 Cr in Q2 FY26. However, EBITDA improved 29% YoY to ₹8 Cr in the quarter under review.

The company attributed the revenue decline to the closure of two Smaaash centres even as margin remained under stress. Meanwhile, Funky Monkey has opened 10 centres in the last 12 months, while plans to open five more centers in FY27.

Meanwhile, Nazara’s adtech arm, comprising Datawrkz and Space & Time, reported a revenue of ₹124 Cr in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA stood at a mere ₹80 Lakhs. The company said that Datawrkz’s top line was hit as “anchor client” paused ad spending.

The quarter also saw sports tech business, Sportskeeda, deliver a revenue of ₹23 Cr against a reported negative EBITDA of ₹1.1 Cr. The EBITDA took a hit as the vertical spent ₹1.2 Cr towards acquiring the Mumbai franchise of theIndian Pickleball League and an additional one-time expense of ₹1.5 Cr in Q2 FY27.

Shares of Nazara closed Monday’s trading session 0.37% lower at ₹399.95 on the BSE.

item.title: Paytm Q2 Profit Skyrockets Over 10X YoY To ₹225 Cr, Revenue Up 28%
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Fintech major Paytm’s profit for the September quarter surged to ₹225 Cr, 10.7X from ₹21 Cr in the year-ago quarter.…
item.content:encoded:
Fintech major Paytm’s profit for the September quarter surged to ₹225 Cr, 10.7X from ₹21 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

The company’s profit for the period was also ₹5 Cr higher than the ₹220 Cr net profit raked in the June quarter. Meanwhile, its EBITDA surged 90% YoY to ₹270 Cr

Operating revenue for the quarter surged 28% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹2,648 Cr. Including other income of ₹182 Cr, Paytm’s total income for the quarter stood at ₹2,830 Cr.

Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter also increased 23% YoY to ₹2,531 Cr. Payment processing charges continued to be the biggest expense during the quarter under review and increased 28% YoY to ₹805 Cr.

The company said that its indirect expenses increased 14% YoY to ₹1,209 Cr, but declined to 46% of revenue from 52% a year earlier.

Software, cloud and data centre expenses rose 59% YoY to ₹211 Cr, reflecting higher AI usage, which Paytm expects to continue for another quarter. It attributed the improvement in operating leverage to AI-led efficiencies and slower growth in platform-building costs relative to revenue.

The company also incorporated ₹3 Cr share of loss from a joint venture during the quarter under review and a ₹4 Cr exceptional item charge which came at the behest of “written-off obsolete capital work-in-progress”.

Besides its financial statements, Paytm’s board also approved the following:

  • An additional ₹500 Cr investment in subsidiary Paytm Cloud Technologies Ltd (PCTL) in one or more tranches over the next twelve months. Subsequently, PCTL’s board has also approved an investment of ₹500 Cr in its subsidiary Paytm Singapore to support future requirements of working capital, investments and business expansion.
  • On NPCI’s recent decision to extend UPI MDR implementation to post Diwali, Paytm said that it expects an indicative uplift of about 2.5 bps in overall Payments Processing Margin. “We expect the actual outcome may stabilise in 2–3 quarters post implementation,” the company added.
  • The fintech major revised its default loss guarantees (DLG) for lending partner Piramal and KSF to ₹150 Cr from ₹90 Cr, up to ₹100 Cr for Vivriti and Ugro, where it had disclosed DLG of up to ₹350 Cr and Muthoot Fincorp Limited of up to ₹90 Cr.

With that, here’s a look at some of the key operational updates for Paytm in the September quarter.

Paytm Q2 Operational Updates

The fintech company continued to expand its payments and financial services distribution business in Q2 FY27 and reported gains in payment processing margins as well as continued its AI investment spree to enhance consumer engagement.

Merchant payments has continued to be the key business growth driver. Paytm’s merchant gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 26% YoY to ₹7.1 Lakh Cr in the September quarter while subscription-paying merchant base grew by 27 Lakh YoY to 1.64 Cr. The company said high merchant retention and subsequent loan distribution were contributing to higher revenue per merchant.

Net payment revenue, excluding the Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) incentive, rose 21% YoY to ₹644 Cr on a comparable basis, while reported growth stood at 8%.

The company said that it received a PIDF incentive of ₹12 Cr in the quarter as against ₹74 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Therefore, its operating revenue, minus the PIDF incentive, grew 33% YoY to ₹2,636 Cr, it claimed.

Meanwhile, Paytm’s payment processing margins expanded by more than four basis points due to a higher share of merchant transactions through credit cards on UPI and Paytm Postpaid, market share gains and pricing discipline.

Paytm Postpaid, its credit line on UPI product, recorded higher sign-ups, increased spending per customer, improved portfolio performance and better profitability following its relaunch. The company expects the product to contribute meaningfully to revenue and EBITDA from FY28 onwards. It also reported improved monetisation through margin trading funding (MTF) and Paytm Gold.

Besides, Paytm’s financial services distribution also expanded. Revenue from the business increased 49% YoY to ₹912 Cr. The number of key financial services customers rose by 2.3 Lakh, or 35%, to 8.8 Lakh. More than half of merchant loan disbursements went to repeat borrowers, reflecting continued engagement and demand among existing customers.

Its merchant loan distribution is also benefiting from a wider pool of eligible borrowers, increased disbursements by lending partners and stable portfolio performance. It is also expanding into higher-ticket loans for merchants using electronic data capture (EDC) devices.

Paytm also continued to gain share in consumer payments. Its monthly transacting users (MTUs) increased by 1 Cr YoY to 8.5 Cr, highest YoY jump in nearly three years. The company’s UPI gross transaction value grew 42% YoY, compared with 19% growth for the industry, marking its sixth consecutive quarter of consumer payment market share gains.

This growth gives it a substantial base for the gains it could potentially realise from the UPI MDR. However, it said that its core business moat doesn’t rely on the discount rate.

“Our business model is to acquire customers through payments and monetise through financial services and technology services. We do not depend on UPI MDR for profitable growth; any MDR on UPI would be an upside, not its foundation,” the company noted.

Shares of Paytm ended today’s trading session 2.67% higher at ₹1,655 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Tata Communications To Pour Up To $450 Mn To Build AI Connectivity Infrastructure
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Tata Communications plans to invest $400-450 Mn (around ₹4,350 Cr) to build 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure across India…
item.content:encoded:
Tata Communications plans to invest $400-450 Mn (around ₹4,350 Cr) to build 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure across India in a bid to capitalise on rising demand for data centre connectivity and compute infrastructure.

The investment will be used to build a new high-speed fibre network connecting major data centres and AI hubs, allowing transfer of large amounts of data faster with minimal delays. The network will also connect to Tata Communications’ existing global network.

The company plans to add around 6 petabits per second (pbps) of network capacity under the programme, taking its total capacity to approximately 7.25 pbps once the expansion is completed. The proposed capacity addition is scheduled between FY30-36 and will be financed via operating cash flows.

Its existing network capacity utilisation stands at around 70%-80%.

Tata Communications said the investment will help it cater to demand from hyperscalers, AI platforms, cloud providers, global capability centres (GCCs), enterprises and digital-native businesses.

The network is designed to support the high capacity, reliability and low latency required to move data between computing infrastructure and data centres.

The first phase will focus on the Mumbai-Pune-Hyderabad-Chennai corridor, one of India’s key AI and hyperscale growth routes. Subsequent phases will extend connectivity to emerging data centre clusters in other parts of the country as well.

The expansion is expected to connect India’s key AI and data centre hubs with international cable landing stations, strengthening connectivity between domestic infrastructure and global AI hubs and allowing for large volumes of data to be shared quickly and reliably between computing facilities. 

“The AI economy needs more than compute. It needs a network built for speed, scale and resilience,” said Tata Communications’ CPTO Rupesh Chokshi.

E2E Networks To Add Compute Capacity

The announcement comes as Indian infrastructure providers step up investments to support growing demand for AI training and inference workloads.

Earlier today, cloud and AI infrastructure provider E2E Networks announced plans to expand its AI factory capacity by nearly 59%, adding around 5.4 megawatts (MW) of capacity through NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other Blackwell GPUs.

The proposed expansion will take E2E Networks’ AI factory capacity to approximately 14.6 MW. The company said the additional capacity will support large-scale model training, post-training, production inference, agentic AI and multimodal applications.

The company is seeing demand from foundation model builders, AI-native startups, enterprises, higher education and research institutions, and public-sector programmes. It also highlighted growing demand for AI infrastructure hosted in India, particularly among organisations operating in regulated and data-sensitive environments.

“India’s AI builders are moving beyond the pilot stage. They now are actively consuming AI tokens in production at previously unheard of scales,” said Tarun Dua, founder and managing director of E2E Networks.

This capacity expansion comes on the back of heightened demand for E2E Networks’ GPU services. Its operating revenue jumped 411% to ₹223.8 Cr in the second quarter of FY27 from ₹43.8 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

It posted a consolidated net profit of ₹72.7 Cr during the quarter under review, reversing a net loss of ₹13.5 Cr a year earlier. It also signed a multi-year cloud GPU contract worth approximately ₹1,000 Cr during the quarter.

item.title: Exclusive: axiTrust To Raise $5 Mn From Argor.vc, Others
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Fintech startup axiTrust is in talks to raise around $5 Mn in fresh capital in its Series A funding round,…
item.content:encoded:
Fintech startup axiTrust is in talks to raise around $5 Mn in fresh capital in its Series A funding round, people aware of the matter told Inc42 on the condition of anonymity. 

The fresh round is likely to be led by Singapore based Argor.vc, and will see participation from axiTrust’s existing investor General Catalyst. 

Questions sent to axiTrust didn’t elicit any response at the time of publishing the story. 

The fresh round has come almost a year after the startup raised $2.6 Mn in its seed funding round led by General Catalyst. Other investors  including Atrium Angels, YAN Network and Supermorpheous are also on the fintech startup’s cap table. 

The fresh capital will help the startup build digital infrastructure to accelerate adoption of its surety bonds offering.

For context, surety bonds are insurance-backed guarantees that assure a buyer or project owner that a business will fulfil its contractual obligations. Instead of blocking the capital as collateral, they allow the buyers to pay a premium to secure the guarantee, helping free up working capital and reduce financial strain.

Founded in 2024  by Aditya Tulsian (CEO), Rajeev Chari (COO), and Mukund Daga (CRO), axiTrust issues, underwrites and manages digital surety bonds, providing an alternative to traditional, collateral-heavy bank guarantees. 

As per the startup, more than ₹15 Lakh Cr of MSME working capital is locked up as collateral for bank guarantees, and replacing these traditional guarantees with insurance-backed digital surety bonds can free that capital, expand credit access, and improve trust in business transactions.

From digital underwriting and AI-based risk assessment to cashflow-based lending and embedded finance, they are filling long-standing gaps that traditional banks could not address efficiently. These solutions are helping businesses and consumers access credit with fewer delays, lighter paperwork, and better transparency.

 Investors are actively backing such startups because the lending market in India is massive, still underserved, and primed for digital disruption offering both strong growth potential and meaningful financial inclusion.

As per Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026, the fintech sector saw funding of $243 Mn across 13 deals. Of these, the heavy lifting was done by lendingtech startup Centricity ₹280 Cr round and Navi’s $100 Mn pre-IPO funding.

item.title: Exclusive: AI-Powered Trading Platform Tradl Bags $4.1 Mn From Nexus, Stellaris
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Bengaluru-based AI-powered trading platform Tradl has raised $4.1 Mn (about ₹40 Cr) in a seed funding round from Nexus Venture…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based AI-powered trading platform Tradl has raised $4.1 Mn (about ₹40 Cr) in a seed funding round from Nexus Venture Partners and Stellaris Venture Partners, sources told Inc42.

The funding round also saw participation from a few angel investors, the sources added.

The startup’s MCA filing further confirmed the fundraise.

Questions sent to Tradl, Stellaris Venture Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners didn’t elicit any response till the time of publishing this story. 


Founded in 2025 by Shubham Bansal and Nilesh Raj, Tradl combines AI with quantitative analysis to help retail traders identify opportunities, analyse stocks, and test trading strategies.

The cofounders are IIT Guwahati graduates. Bansal previously spent around five years at Goldman Sachs, while Raj worked at fintech startup Stable Money. 

Bringing AI To Trading

Tradl’s toolkit includes an AI-powered stock screener, technical charts, and backtesting tools that allow users to test trading strategies against historical market data. It also helps traders track sector rotation and monitor corporate events that could influence stock prices.

The startup lists chart pattern alerts, broader market insights, and personalised option chains among its other tools, although these are marked as available through private access on its website.

According to Tradl, its AI interprets natural-language queries and translates them into instructions for its quantitative engine. The engine then processes market data using fixed rules to generate consistent results for the same query and dataset. 


The startup’s stated aim is to give retail traders access to the depth of analysis typically available to institutional trading desks. It lists the NSE, the BSE, and the MCX as exchange partners, and CMOTS as a data partner on its website.

Tradl’s fundraise comes amid growing investment in Indian AI startups. The segment attracted $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY, making it the most-funded sector during the quarter.

AI is also becoming a feature of platforms serving retail investors and traders. Investment and stock broking platform Trackk raised $3.7 Mn in a seed round led by Lightspeed, with participation from Info Edge Ventures, earlier this year. The startup offers AI-led stock discovery alongside broking, derivatives trading, and portfolio tracking tools.

More recently, IPO-bound investment advisory platform StockGro raised ₹110 Cr from existing backers as part of its ongoing Series B round. StockGro combines investment research and trading insights with AI-powered research tools.

item.title: Pronto Founder Anjali Sardana Sets Up Physical AI Venture Provision Labs In US
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Instant home services startup Pronto’s founder Anjali Sardana has launched Provision Labs, a physical AI venture based in San Francisco.…
item.content:encoded:
Instant home services startup Pronto’s founder Anjali Sardana has launched Provision Labs, a physical AI venture based in San Francisco.

According to its website, Provision Labs will collect data to train and test AI systems designed to perform real-world tasks using robots and other machines. It will work with developers building physical AI models.

The development was first reported by Economic Times. Provision Labs plans to source training data from professionals across sectors globally and help AI developers deploy their models, the report said.

Sardana will serve as the CEO of Provision Labs as well as Pronto.

The launch comes months after Pronto faced scrutiny over a pilot involving recordings of household chores to generate training data for physical AI and robotics systems. 

The issue came to light after Entrackr reported that Pronto was exploring the use of footage from household tasks to generate real-world training data for robotics labs. Investor documents reviewed by the publication stated that the startup was building a data business by leveraging its workforce to capture household activities and had begun piloting real-world training data with leading physical AI labs.

During the pilot, Pronto’s service professionals wore cameras while doing household chores such as washing dishes, folding laundry, cleaning and preparing meals.

Pronto later told Inc42 that the pilot was voluntary and only available to customers who opted in while booking a service. The startup said the pilot covered less than 0.01% of its users at the time.

“Pronto does not, by default, record in customers’ homes, nor does it use customer data. We started the pilot you are referring to a few days ago. It is a strictly opt-in feature, available only to customers who actively choose it at the time of booking,” the startup said back then.

Pronto also said participating customers paid for the feature and could access anonymised footage on the app for 48 hours. It maintained that the footage would not be shared with third-party AI labs and would be deleted from its servers within 48 hours.

In a subsequent social media post, the startup said it had spent months working towards compliance with India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act. It argued that real-world behavioural data would be essential to training robots to operate in household environments.

However, the pilot drew criticism over whether customers fully understood how recordings made inside their homes could be used to develop physical AI systems. Questions also emerged around data storage, processing and the extent to which such footage could be used to build commercial training datasets.

Physical AI Creates Demand For Real-World Training Data

Provision Labs’ launch comes amid growing demand for real-world data to train robots to manipulate objects, navigate different environments, and perform everyday tasks.

Startups are already tapping India’s workforce to build these datasets. Y Combinator-backed Human Archive collects recordings of workers performing physical tasks, processes the footage, and sells the resulting datasets to frontier AI labs and robotics companies.

The likes of Awign, Objectways, and Human Archive are building pipelines to supply first-person footage of human activity to AI developers. However, the opportunity raises questions around workers’ consent and compensation, the privacy of others captured on camera, and how much value Indian data suppliers retain when the resulting models and intellectual property belong to overseas companies.

item.title: Pune Police Ask Google, Apple To Remove Rapido App Over Bike Taxi Operations
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Pune Police has written to Google and Apple seeking the removal of Rapido’s app from their respective app stores over…
item.content:encoded:
Pune Police has written to Google and Apple seeking the removal of Rapido’s app from their respective app stores over its alleged unauthorised bike taxi operations in the city.

Pune Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar told the Times of India that communications had been sent to the two companies requesting the app’s removal.

Inc42 has reached out to Rapido for comment. The story will be updated on receiving a response.

The move follows an FIR against Rapido’s parent entity, Roppen Transportation Services Pvt Ltd, for allegedly operating bike taxi services without the required licence and regulatory approvals. The FIR was registered at Vishrantwadi police station following an enforcement drive by the Pune Regional Transport Office (RTO).

Earlier, Pune district collector and Regional Transport Authority (RTA) chairperson Jitendra Dudi had directed Rapido to suspend its bike taxi operations across Pune district until it secured an ebike taxi aggregator licence.

According to TOI, Rapido’s application for permission to operate bike taxis remains pending with the transport department.

The FIR alleges that Rapido facilitated paid passenger rides on two-wheelers registered as non-transport vehicles. The alleged violation came to light when Pune RTO motor vehicle inspector Prasad Govardhan Surwase booked a ride through the app during the enforcement drive.

It also refers to an October 15 notice warning the platform against unauthorised operations and an earlier notice issued by the Transport Commissioner’s Office on April 29, 2025.

According to the FIR, Rapido applied for an aggregator licence with the Transport Commissioner’s Office in Mumbai on August 11, 2026, but the application remained pending at the time of the alleged violation.

The complaint also alleges inadequate driver background checks, raising concerns about passenger safety, particularly for women.

Wider Scrutiny Of Aggregators

Separately, Dudi directed cab aggregators to submit monthly fare data to the district administration and display RTA-approved fares separately on their apps, following complaints from autorickshaw and cab drivers about alleged fare violations.

According to Dudi, drivers must receive 80% of the RTA base fare, while passenger fares can range from 50% below the base fare to 1.5 times that amount. Complaints about driver underpayment and passengers being charged beyond the permitted range prompted the monthly reporting requirement.

The directions followed a meeting with representatives of driver unions and aggregators. Dudi warned of legal action over continued unauthorised bike taxi operations and said Rapido could not resume the service without a licence. 

Rapido’s efforts to secure permission to operate in Pune date back to 2022, when its licence application was rejected, triggering proceedings before the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court.

In January 2023, the Bombay High Court directed Rapido to stop operating its app. The following month, the SC disposed of the related petitions, allowing the platform to approach the High Court to challenge Maharashtra’s January 2023 notification prohibiting the aggregation and pooling of rides using non-transport vehicles.

item.title: Aequs Q2: Loss Widens 2.5X To ₹52.4 Cr, Revenue Jumps 45% YoY
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Contract manufacturing company Aequs reported a consolidated net loss of ₹52.4 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, widening 154.4%…
item.content:encoded:
Contract manufacturing company Aequs reported a consolidated net loss of ₹52.4 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, widening 154.4% from ₹20.6 Cr in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. 

Operating revenue climbed 45.3% to ₹409.1 Cr from ₹281.6 Cr.

Sequentially, revenue increased 3.4% from ₹395.5 Cr, while net loss narrowed marginally from ₹53.2 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Including other income of ₹10.6 Cr, Aequs’ total income stood at ₹419.7 Cr during the quarter under review.

However, expenses excluding finance costs, depreciation, and amortisation rose faster than revenue, increasing 56.2% to ₹395.2 Cr from ₹253.1 Cr a year earlier.

EBITDA for the quarter under review fell 45% YoY to ₹24.5 Cr but rose 14% sequentially.

Constituting 85.9% to the topline, Aequs’ aerospace business remained its main revenue contributor, generating ₹351.4 Cr during the quarter, up 44.2% from ₹243.7 Cr a year earlier.

The company said that its aerospace order book reached $1.1 Bn, growing 9% QoQ. During said that the Safran A320 wheels agreement marks Aequs’ first serial-production contract

Meanwhile, consumer business revenue increased 52% to ₹57.7 Cr from ₹37.9 Cr. 

Executive chairman and CEO Aravind Melligeri highlighted a slow down in Q2 volume ramp in the consumer business due to extended qualification timelines and supply chain constraints.

“We view this as a timing-related shift rather than a change in the underlying opportunity, with customer programs continuing to progress. Given these factors, we are recalibrating the path to consumer EBITDA breakeven, with our near-term focus on improving utilisation and translating installed capacity into profitable growth,” he added.

During the quarter, the company signed new long-term supply agreements, expanding its relationships to six Safran entities and broadening its manufacturing scope across critical aerospace components. It is currently leveraging Belagavi manufacturing and working on completion of its upcoming Hosur manufacturing ecosystem.

For this, the company’s promoter group recently infused ₹650 Cr by subscribing to preferential warrants to fuel its next phase of capacity expansion, bolster strategic JV investments and cater to certain working capital requirements.

“To support this next phase of growth, we continue to invest in our manufacturing capabilities. H1 FY27 capital expenditure stood at ₹159.7 Cr, and the ₹650 Cr promoter warrant is intended to support the next phase of expansion, including Hosur. Following quarter-end, new Safran agreements expanded our relationships to six entities. As these capabilities and partnerships grow, our focus remains on disciplined execution and stronger returns,” Melligeri added.

Shares of Aequs ended today’s trading session 2.74% higher at ₹242.10 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Announcing FAST42 2027: The Hunt For India’s 42 Fastest-Growing D2C Brands Begins
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42

item.content:encoded:
India’s D2C ecosystem has no shortage of new brands. But as competition intensifies, identifying the businesses delivering strong revenue growth, beyond the attention generated by funding announcements, product launches and marketing campaigns, is becoming increasingly important.

This is the premise behind FAST42, Inc42’s annual ranking of India’s fastest-growing D2C brands. Now in its sixth edition, FAST42 2027 invites applications from emerging consumer brands to identify and rank 42 businesses by verified revenue growth between FY24 and FY26.

Since 2022, FAST42 has been part of Inc42’s broader effort to identify, track and recognise emerging consumer businesses. Backed by more than a decade of startup ecosystem coverage, sector research and engagement with D2C founders, the initiative has consistently focused on a measurable indicator of business growth: revenue.

The numbers from previous editions illustrate the scale of businesses featured in the ranking. The FAST42 2026 cohort, selected from over 250 applications, comprised 42 brands that collectively generated ₹2,154 Cr in annual revenue and employed more than 6,700 people.

Over the years, FAST42 has recognised brands such as Pilgrim, The Sleep Company, Snitch, Sweet Karam Coffee, Beco, Perfora, XYXX, Innovist, Fix My Curls and The Pant Project, among others.

These brands represent a cross-section of India’s consumer economy, spanning established categories, emerging niches and different approaches to building and scaling a business.

With FAST42 2027, Inc42 is looking to identify the next set of emerging brands demonstrating exceptional revenue growth.

Presented by Inc42 and Shadowfax, and co-presented by PhonePe Payment Gateway, the sixth edition will culminate in the unveiling of India’s 42 fastest-growing eligible D2C brands in February 2027.

Apply For FAST42 2027

India’s D2C Market Is Growing. So Is The Competition.

India’s D2C market is entering a period of significant expansion. According to Inc42’s D2C 3.0: The Next Big Wave In Indian Ecommerce Report 2026, India’s D2C gross merchandise value (GMV) is projected to grow from $65 Bn in 2026 to $310 Bn by 2031, clocking a CAGR of approximately 37%.

This compares with a projected 22% CAGR for the broader ecommerce market. D2C channels are also expected to account for nearly 86% of the incremental GMV added by India’s ecommerce sector over the next five years.

However, the changing retail landscape is also making growth more complex.

Performance marketing and online marketplaces, which powered India’s first wave of digital-first brands, are increasingly being complemented by quick commerce and offline retail. Brands now have more ways to reach consumers, but must also manage competition across channels, customer acquisition costs, repeat purchases and distribution economics.

As India’s D2C ecosystem moves into this next phase, the distinction between building brand visibility and translating consumer demand into revenue growth becomes more relevant.

FAST42 2027 will spotlight brands that have demonstrated this growth, regardless of the categories they operate in or the combination of channels driving their sales.

How Will FAST42 2027 Identify The Fastest-Growing Brands?

FAST42 is a data-led ranking, with growth determined by financial performance rather than funding, valuations or brand popularity.

For its 2027 edition, Inc42 will rank 42 eligible D2C brands on their compound annual revenue growth rate (CAGR) between FY24 and FY26.

Inc42’s team of editors, reporters and analysts will review applications and verify the financial information provided by shortlisted brands before determining the final ranking.

The ranking will also document the selected brands’ business journeys, offering insights into the categories, strategies, and markets driving their expansion.

Apply For FAST42 2027

What Does Making The FAST42 List Mean For Brands?

Beyond the ranking itself, FAST42 provides emerging consumer brands with a platform to bring their growth stories to a wider audience.

Previous editions have featured businesses across food and beverages, fashion, beauty and personal care, wellness, home products and other consumer categories, highlighting the breadth of brands gaining scale in India.

For brands selected in FAST42 2027, the initiative offers:

  • Recognition For Verified Growth: A place among India’s 42 fastest-growing eligible D2C brands, determined through a consistent, revenue-based ranking methodology.
  • Visibility Across Inc42’s Platforms: A feature in FAST42’s interactive online ranking and an exclusive coffee table book documenting the selected businesses.
  • A Platform For Their Growth Stories: Opportunities for Inc42’s editorial team to examine the founders, business models and strategies behind standout brands.
  • Access To The Wider Ecosystem: Recognition at the FAST42 Conclave and visibility among investors, business partners, industry leaders and prospective talent.

For emerging brands navigating their next stage of expansion, FAST42 offers an independent distinction based on their financial performance and an opportunity to bring their businesses to the attention of a larger industry audience.

FAST42 2027 Applications Close On 10 December

Applications for FAST42 2027 are open until 10 December 2026.

The final ranking will be unveiled at the FAST42 Conclave in Delhi NCR in February 2027, bringing together the selected brands, D2C founders, investors and other stakeholders from India’s consumer ecosystem.

The 42 ranked brands will also be featured on Inc42’s website and in the FAST42 coffee table book.

As India’s D2C market continues to expand, FAST42 2027 aims to identify the emerging brands turning that market opportunity into measurable growth.

If your brand has demonstrated exceptional revenue growth between FY24 and FY26, applications for FAST42 2027 are now open.

Applicants must be able to substantiate their revenue figures with supporting financial documents. With no jury selections or paid placements, every position on the FAST42 list is earned through verified revenue growth.

item.title: Exclusive: Imarticus Eyes Confidential Filing In 2-3 Months For ₹1,000 Cr IPO
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Edtech startup Imarticus Learning plans to file its DRHP with SEBI through the confidential route within the next two to…
item.content:encoded:
Edtech startup Imarticus Learning plans to file its DRHP with SEBI through the confidential route within the next two to three months for a ₹1,000 Cr IPO, sources told Inc42. 

The proposed issue size has increased from the ₹750 Cr planned earlier, which was to comprise a mix of fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS).

Imarticus intends to use proceeds from the IPO to expand its existing business and pursue acquisitions, the sources added.

Its organic expansion could include setting up more Centres of Excellence (CoEs), expanding offerings at the Imarticus School of Finance and Business (ISFB), and strengthening its B2B business, they said.

Inc42 has reached out to Imarticus for comment on its IPO plans. The story will be updated on receiving a response.

Expanding Ahead Of IPO

The IPO preparations follow Imarticus’ recent ₹800 Cr acquisition of Singapore’s BELLS Institute of Higher Learning, aimed at expanding its presence in Singapore and Southeast Asia.

The acquisition also strengthened its capabilities in enterprise learning, AI, data analytics, technology, and workforce development. Imarticus plans to launch the BELLS School of AI, offering courses in machine learning, AI applications in finance and fintech, and business transformation.

The startup also inaugurated a Centre of Excellence for the Indian capital market in August. This followed the launch of ISFB last year, with an inaugural undergraduate cohort of 50 students.

Founded in 2012 by Nikhil Barshikar and Sonya Hooja, Mumbai-based Imarticus offers professional education and upskilling programmes across finance, banking, analytics, technology, marketing, and management.

Its business spans B2C programmes for students and working professionals, alongside enterprise training, e-learning, and workforce development solutions.

Last year, the startup acquired edtech platform MyCaptain in a ₹50 Cr cash and stock deal to broaden its course offerings, drawing on the latter’s expertise in digital marketing.

The planned offering follows PhysicsWallah’s ₹3,480 Cr IPO in November 2025. Meanwhile, Fusion Klassroom Edutech listed on the BSE SME platform in August 2026 following its ₹39.04 Cr IPO.

Imarticus’ IPO preparations come amid a prolonged funding slowdown and consolidation in the edtech sector. Last month, upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy in a deal valuing the latter at just over $200 Mn, down more than 90% from its peak valuation of $3.5 Bn.

item.title: MakeMyTrip Swings To $1.8 Mn Profit In Q2 FY27, Revenue Up 2.5% YoY
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Nasdaq-listed online travel major MakeMyTrip swung to a consolidated net profit of $1.8 Mn in the September quarter of FY27…
item.content:encoded:
Nasdaq-listed online travel major MakeMyTrip swung to a consolidated net profit of $1.8 Mn in the September quarter of FY27 from a loss of $5.7 Mn a year earlier, helped by higher operating profit and lower net finance costs.

Revenue rose 2.5% to $235.2 Mn from $229.3 Mn in Q2 FY26. On a constant currency basis, which excludes the impact of exchange rate movements, revenue grew 11.2%.

The company said the rupee depreciated approximately 10% against the dollar compared with the year-ago quarter, weighing on its reported revenue and growth rates.

Meanwhile, international long-haul outbound travel from India continued to remain subdued as elevated fuel prices pushed up airfares and a weaker rupee increased the overall cost of overseas trips. Domestic travel demand partially offset these pressures, the company said.

Operationally, the company’s gross bookings increased 11.3% YoY to $2.72 Bn during the quarter. 

Hotels and packages remained MakeMyTrip’s largest revenue contributor, bringing in $107.1 Mn in Q2 FY27, down 1% from $108.2 Mn a year earlier. The segment includes customer inducement costs of $50.7 Mn in the quarter under review.

Meanwhile, bus ticketing revenue climbed 16.6% to $39.1 Mn from $33.5 Mn. A 24.7% increase in the number of bus tickets drove gross bookings in the segment up 20% to $435.3 Mn.

The “others” segment, which MMT said was led by ancillary services and car bookings, posted revenue of $32.3 Mn, up 21.6% YoY.

On the expense front, MMT said that its service cost fell 4.6% to $49.2 Mn from $51.5 Mn a year ago, on the back of rupee weakening against the dollar. Strong demand for its car booking business in India partly offset the decline. 

Personnel expenses dropped 4.9% to $38.4 Mn from $40.4 Mn, again largely due to the weaker rupee, along with lower share-based compensation costs. Annual wage hikes in the June quarter partly offset the fall, the company added.

Marketing and sales promotion expenses rose 2.6% to $38.9 Mn from $37.9 Mn, driven by higher variable costs and discretionary spends such as events and brand-building. Separately, customer inducement costs, which MMT records as a reduction of revenue, rose to $108.9 Mn from $89.1 Mn.

item.title: Veefin H1 FY27 Profit Jumps 2.3X YoY To ₹25 Cr, Revenue More Than Doubles
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Ahead of listing on the mainboard, BSE SME-listed fintech SaaS company Veefin Solutions reported a 127% rise in its consolidated…
item.content:encoded:
Ahead of listing on the mainboard, BSE SME-listed fintech SaaS company Veefin Solutions reported a 127% rise in its consolidated net profit to ₹24.9 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹11 Cr in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. The company’s net profit also increased 9% from ₹22.8 Cr in the preceding six months.

Operating revenue more than doubled to ₹238.8 Cr in the first half of FY27 from ₹110.4 Cr a year earlier. This was also 3% higher than the ₹232.7 Cr recorded in H2 FY26.

Including other income of ₹1.8 Cr, Veefin’s total income stood at ₹240.6 Cr in H1 FY27, compared with ₹112.1 Cr a year earlier.

Total expenses increased 109% to ₹205.3 Cr from ₹98 Cr.

For Q2 FY27, Veefin’s net profit rose 61% to ₹15.3 Cr from ₹9.5 Cr in the preceding quarter. Operating revenue increased 9% QoQ to ₹124.7 Cr from ₹114.2 Cr, while total income stood at ₹125.7 Cr.

The company’s consolidated EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, rose 160% to ₹60.8 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹23.4 Cr in the year-ago period. Its EBITDA margin expanded to 25.5% from 21.2%, an improvement of 424 basis points. The consolidated profit margin also increased to 10.4% from 9.9%.

On a standalone basis, Veefin reported operating revenue of ₹49.2 Cr in H1 FY27, up 83.6% from ₹26.8 Cr a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to ₹27.2 Cr from ₹13.1 Cr, while net profit rose 79.4% to ₹14 Cr from ₹7.8 Cr.

Important to highlight that the SME company secured an in-principle approval from the BSE’s Internal Regulatory Oversight and Review Group (IRORG) to migrate its shares from the exchange’s SME Platform to the mainboard. It is yet to receive a go-ahead from the NSE for the migration.

Veefin’s Growing Business Pipeline

Beyond its financial performance, Veefin reported an open business pipeline of ₹920 Cr at the end of the September quarter, up from ₹760 Cr at the end of the preceding quarter. The company added ₹240 Cr in new opportunities during the quarter, while ₹46 Cr was converted into contracted business. Other movements reduced the pipeline by a net ₹35 Cr.

The pipeline comprises 77 deals across 16 countries in five regions. According to the investor presentation, 75% of the pipeline is qualified, while 11% is under negotiation. The company also reported recent wins involving a leading finance company and two public sector banks (PSBs) in India.

Supply chain finance (SCF) accounts for 35% of the pipeline value, followed by digital lending at 23%, trade and cash management at 18%, and digital banking at 16%. Fraud and risk management contributes 3%, while other products account for the remaining 5%.

The company has expanded beyond its bread and butter SCF, with 65% of the open pipeline value coming from offering beyond SCF. Further, 38 of the 77 deals involve customers evaluating more than one product, indicating opportunities to sell multiple solutions to the same customer.’

Veefin’s broader product portfolio includes supply chain finance, trade finance, cash and liquidity management, loan origination and management, debt collections, corporate and retail internet banking, mobile banking, fraud management, risk analytics and financing infrastructure. The latter includes its PSB Xchange Marketplace, guarantee management and TReDS technology.

International markets account for 84% of the pipeline value. Southeast Asia contributes 56%, followed by India at 16%, the rest of South Asia at 12%, the Middle East at 11%, Africa at 3% and Europe at 2%. India accounts for the largest number of deals, at 32%, followed by Southeast Asia at 29%.

Existing customers contributed 73.9% of standalone revenue during the first half, with new customers accounting for the remaining 26.1%. In Q2 FY27, the corresponding shares were 69.9% and 30.1%, respectively.

Shares of Veefin ended today’s trading session 14.89% higher at ₹245.30 apiece on the BSE.
